correct_answer: Escalate to VP Sales (James Park) for approval - while the January DM delegation exists, the condition was to "tag me in #deal-desk for visibility" which wasn't done, making the delegation incomplete
rationale: The correct answer is A. While Sarah Kim did receive delegation authority from James Park for co-term deals under $500K (covering this $340K deal), the delegation came with an explicit condition: "Just tag me in #deal-desk so I have visibility." This wasn't done - there's no mention of James in the #deal-desk thread about this deal. Delegated authority with conditions requires ALL conditions to be met. Option A ignores the Confluence policy requiring CFO approval for co-terms. Option B misses that the informal January delegation from VP Sales (who has authority to interpret policy for his org) takes precedence over the formal policy for Q1, especially given the "Finance is overwhelmed" context. Option C is wrong because retroactive tagging doesn't provide the required visibility before approval - James needed to see it during the approval process, not after. The delegation was conditional, not absolute. Marcus should have tagged James on March 15, and since he didn't, the deal needs to go to James now for proper approval. This tests understanding that informal delegations can override formal policies BUT only when all stated conditions are met, and that visibility requirements in fast-moving sales orgs are substantive, not procedural.
